title: Self-employed health insurance deduction: who qualifies
label: Gig worker money tip

lines: Omar left his job to drive full-time.
Now he buys his own health plan.

items.l: Could join a spouse's work plan

beats.note: Limited by the profit from that business.

cta.sub: We'll DM you how to book a call.

captions.instagram:
Self-employed and paying for your own health insurance? The premiums may be deductible.

✔️ You need a business profit. The deduction is limited by the profit from that business (Form 7206).
✔️ It doesn't apply for any month you could have joined an employer-subsidized plan, including your spouse's, even if you didn't sign up.
✔️ It can cover you, your spouse, your dependents and children under 27.
✔️ It goes on Schedule 1 of Form 1040, so you don't have to itemize.

Not sure if you qualify? Book a call and we'll check.

captions.youtube_description: Self-employed people with a business profit can often deduct health insurance premiums for themselves, a spouse, dependents and children under 27, on Schedule 1 (Form 7206). Not for any month you could join an employer-subsidized plan, including a spouse's. The deduction is limited by the profit from that business.

sources.fact: Self-employed health insurance deduction: Schedule C/F net profit, partners with SE earnings, >2% S corp shareholders; no deduction for any month you were eligible for an employer-subsidized plan (incl. spouse's employer); can cover children under 27; Form 7206 uses net profit from the business as a limit; Schedule 1 line 17 (2025 instructions and 2026 draft); read 2026-10-30
